title: MemSens: Significantly Reducing Memory Overhead in Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis Using Novel Error-Bounded Lossy Compression
problem: Adjoint sensitivity analysis requires storing all state vectors and Jacobian matrices at every time step for gradient computation, leading to prohibitive memory costs for large-scale dynamic systems and long simulations.
motivation: Adjoint methods are efficient for computing gradients in circuit design and verification, but memory overhead proportional to system size and time steps limits applicability to large problems.
method: Compresses the state information needed for adjoint calculations using specialized algorithms that recognize patterns in how circuit simulation data changes across different circuit parts and over time. The compression is lossy—it throws away some information—but error-bounded, so it only discards information in carefully controlled ways that won't break the final gradient calculation. This cuts memory requirements while keeping numerical accuracy.
key_novelty: First adjoint method using lossy compression with error bounds to reduce memory without sacrificing numerical accuracy.
contributions: Two-order-of-magnitude (100x) reduction in memory overhead during simulation
Preserves accuracy of adjoint solutions despite lossy compression
Leverages spatiotemporal data characteristics for effective compression
limitations: Not discussed; applicability to non-circuit simulation domains unclear.
